title: 2. Force them to be honest about their motives.
use_cases: Use when drafting the inciting incident to ensure the protagonist has skin in the game
Implement when a character's actions feel passive or dictated by the plot rather than internal desire
Configure when bridging the gap between a character's professional task and their personal obsession
content: Identify why the protagonist wants that goal. This is where the sense of agency often falls flat, because the protagonist doesn’t really want what they spend all novel going after. They have surface motives, such as “save the world,” but if you ask them why, they shrug and answer, “Reasons.” Did Daniel care if the Air Force solved the mystery of the stargate? No. He just wanted to get paid (at first). But the more he learned about it, the more it connected to his dream. He pursued the plot’s goals because they led him toward his own personal dream of figuring out who built the pyramids.(Here’s more on What's My Motivation? Tips on Showing Character Motivations)
